selection.rule: Projects of construction-progress.json (plot-level pin) whose Sentinel-2 series had a clear view in fewer than 75% of months: clouds hide them too often for the optical series alone.

band_rule: 90th percentile of the absolute month-to-month change of the index over all 1089 month pairs of all projects

source.name: Copernicus Sentinel-1 radar, Radiometrically Terrain Corrected (RTC) by Catalyst, hosted by Microsoft Planetary Computer
source.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Microsoft Planetary Computer, sentinel-1-rtc). Copernicus Sentinel data are free and open (EU Regulation 1159/2013).
source.attribution: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2023-2026, processed by ESA; radiometric terrain correction by Catalyst; hosted by Microsoft Planetary Computer; analysis by Kolaboro

method: Per project, one Sentinel-1 track (the same orbit direction and relative orbit every month, so the viewing angle does not change). Per month, up to 3 scenes spread over the month with valid values for at least 80% of the circle. Per scene, the mean gamma-nought backscatter (linear power) in the 150 m circle around the pin and in a ring 300 to 600 m from it, for VV and VH; per month, the median of the scenes, in decibels. Change index y: (circle minus ring) minus its median over the first 3 months with data, in dB. Rain, wet soil or a different satellite move the circle and the ring together and cancel out; a structure on the plot does not.
limits: Radar sees through cloud and at night. New walls, frames, roofs and cranes usually raise VV (corner reflections); cleared vegetation usually lowers VH. It does not show floors, finishes or quality of work, and a building's orientation to the satellite changes how bright it looks. Pixels are 10 m and speckled, so small plots and single villas may not show. Treat a change as a reason to ask the developer for dated site photos, not as proof.

fields.vv: VV backscatter in the circle, dB
fields.sum: medians of the first and last 3 months with data
